run.question:
payment-service is throwing 500 errors — investigate the root cause using
the app-263-prod-logs index.

report.summary: The only data actually returned in this Run came from the Elasticsearch index app-263-prod-logs (source otel-demo, target m0-otel-20260909) and from the readable Kubernetes cluster; every Prometheus and Jaeger query returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so error rates, latency baselines and traces are unknown (not zero). The index contains 7 documents in the authorized window 2026-11-21T09:59:41Z–2026-11-22T09:59:41Z, dated 2026-11-22T07:59:33Z–09:29:33Z: 4 ERROR, 2 INFO, 1 WARN, spread over three distinct service identities payment-service-us (3), payment-service-eu (2) and payment-service-ap (2). The ERROR texts describe two separate upstream dependencies: payment-service-us logged 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us after 30000ms' at 07:59:33Z and later 'Connection pool exhausted (max=50, active=50)' at 08:59:33Z plus WARN 'Retry queue depth=812' at 09:29:33Z; payment-service-eu logged 'adyen-eu sandbox responded 503 Service Unavailable' at 07:59:33Z and 'Failed to authenticate to adyen-eu: invalid api_key' at 08:59:33Z. payment-service-ap logged only INFO ('Healthy: p95 latency 290ms' and 'Healthy'). No document in the index carries an HTTP 500, so the '500 errors' framing is not itself visible in the logs; what is visible are four ERROR lines naming failures of the two upstream payment providers. Because the failures split across two different providers and instances, the evidence does not converge on a single causative object, so no root cause is asserted; the two provider-level causes are stated as hypotheses and the adyen-eu API-key value could not be read (secrets are unreadable). Separately, I checked the readable cluster: the only payment workload there is Deployment payment in namespace otel-demo (service 'payment', image 2.0.2-payment, 1/1 ready) whose pod payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d is Running and Ready with restartCount 2 and a last termination exitCode 255/reason Unknown at 08:04:13Z; its own logs in the window showed completed transactions and no error-level lines, and its caller checkout logged 'payment went through' repeatedly up to 09:59:16Z. That cluster has no namespace app-263 and no workload named payment-service, and the index documents carry no cluster/region/environment field, so the index entries payment-service-us/-eu/-ap could not be tied to the readable cluster; they are different identities from its 'payment' service. flagd-config shows paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable with defaultVariant 'off', so no fault-injection setting was observed in effect for this cluster.

claims.text: Index app-263-prod-logs holds 7 documents in the window 2026-11-21T09:59:41Z–2026-11-22T09:59:41Z (4 ERROR, 2 INFO, 1 WARN) by services payment-service-us=3, payment-service-eu=2, payment-service-ap=2, with document timestamps from 2026-11-22T07:59:33Z to 2026-11-22T09:29:33Z.
payment-service-us logged ERROR 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us after 30000ms' at 2026-11-22T07:59:33Z.
payment-service-eu logged ERROR 'adyen-eu sandbox responded 503 Service Unavailable' at 2026-11-22T07:59:33Z.
payment-service-us logged ERROR 'Connection pool exhausted (max=50, active=50)' at 2026-11-22T08:59:33Z.
payment-service-eu logged ERROR 'Failed to authenticate to adyen-eu: invalid api_key' at 2026-11-22T08:59:33Z.
payment-service-us logged WARN 'Retry queue depth=812' at 2026-11-22T09:29:33Z, while payment-service-ap logged only INFO ('Healthy: p95 latency 290ms' at 07:59:33Z and 'Healthy' at 09:29:33Z).

The app-263-prod-logs mapping contains only the fields level, message, service and timestamp; the documents carry no cluster, region or environment field, so the logs cannot be tied to a cluster from their own content.

The readable cluster's only payment workload is Deployment payment in namespace otel-demo (1 replica, 1 available, 1 ready, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-payment, env FLAGD_HOST=flagd, FLAGD_PORT=8013), exposed by Service payment with selector opentelemetry.io/name=payment on port 8080; there is no Deployment or Service named payment-service anywhere in the cluster.

Pod payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d (owner ReplicaSet payment-6f7bc865d6) is Running and Ready; its payment container has restartCount 2, and its last state was terminated with exitCode 255, reason Unknown, finishedAt 2026-11-22T08:04:13Z, with the current instance started at 2026-11-22T08:04:20Z.

In the window, the payment pod's current container produced 351 log lines whose only error-matching line is '(node:24) MetadataLookupWarning: received unexpected error = Invalid response from metadata service: incorrect Metadata-Flavor header. code = UNKNOWN' at 2026-11-22T08:04:24Z; a dedicated filter for error-level lines matched only that line, and the other lines are 'Charge request received.' / 'Transaction complete.' entries.
The caller checkout logged 'payment went through (transaction_id: ...)' repeatedly, with the newest shown line at 2026-11-22T09:59:16Z.

ConfigMap flagd-config defines paymentFailure (state ENABLED, defaultVariant 'off', variants 100%/90%/75%/50%/25%/10%/off) and paymentUnreachable (state ENABLED, defaultVariant 'off'), i.e. both payment fault-injection flags read as switched off in the stored configuration.
Cluster namespaces are app-282, default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, otel-demo and opspilot-readonly; no namespace app-263 exists.

The 17 events inside the window contain none involving any payment object; grouped results are Deployment checkout/loki ScalingReplicaSet, Pod checkout-698c8f5df-2z6dv and loki-66445c6d6f-qp9h9 Created/Pulled/Started in app-282, ReplicaSet checkout-698c8f5df and loki-66445c6d6f SuccessfulCreate, plus Warning FailedToCreateEndpoint for Endpoints orca and signup-service.

The Prometheus rule configuration holds a CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh alert (checkout PlaceOrder server-span error ratio > 0.5 for 2m, labels cluster=opspilot-m1, opspilot_integration_id=m0-otel-20260909) and OpsPilot self-monitoring alerts; there is no payment-specific alerting rule in the stored file.

For payment-service-us the most likely mechanism is an upstream stripe-us call stalling to its 30s timeout, which held connections until the 50-connection pool was exhausted (max=50, active=50) and Retry queue depth reached 812, so charge requests on that instance fail; the named dependency stripe-us has no data in any source available in this Run and the index contains no HTTP 500 line, so this remains a hypothesis built from the four log texts.

For payment-service-eu the most likely cause is the adyen-eu upstream: a 503 from the sandbox at 07:59:33Z followed by an authentication failure ('invalid api_key') at 08:59:33Z, meaning the credential used for adyen-eu is rejected; the api_key value itself is a secret that cannot be read, so this cannot be verified, and adyen-eu has no observability data in any source available here.

A single common cause for both regional instances is not supported: the messages name two different providers (stripe-us for payment-service-us, adyen-eu for payment-service-eu) and the two ERROR pairs occur at the same two collection timestamps, which is equally consistent with independent failures logged on the same schedule.

The readable cluster's payment service shows no failure of its own in the window: its Deployment payment is 1/1 ready, its pod payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d is Running/Ready, its error-level log filter matched only a startup MetadataLookupWarning, its log lines are 'Charge request received.'/'Transaction complete.', and its caller checkout logged successful payments through 09:59:16Z.

Fault injection through flagd explaining these errors was considered and not supported for this cluster: paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable both read defaultVariant 'off' in flagd-config, the cluster has no payment-service workload, and the cluster's payment pod logged no error-level line or failed charge.

Restore or point at Prometheus and Jaeger and re-query payment-service-us/-eu error-rate and dependency spans (e.g. traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name=...}, rpc_client_duration for the stripe/adyen calls) to convert the two provider hypotheses into measured causes and to establish a pre-incident baseline.

Have the payment-service-eu owner verify the adyen-eu API key/credential configuration (the stored secret cannot be read here) and the paymentservice-us owner review the 50-connection pool and 30s upstream timeout settings against stripe-us latency before changing anything.

Establish which cluster/environment app-263-prod-logs belongs to and add cluster/region fields to it, since the index documents carry no such field and the names payment-service-us/-eu/-ap have no counterpart in the readable cluster.

gaps: All Prometheus queries (get_metric_names, get_label_values, get_prometheus_target, execute_prometheus_instant_query, list_prometheus_rules) and all Jaeger queries (traces_search, traces_list_services) returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no error rate, latency baseline, span error tags or call graph exist for payment-service-us/-eu/-ap or for the cluster's payment service; these signals are unknown, not zero, and no latency comparison was possible.

A term query for service 'payment-service' and 'payment' in app-263-prod-logs returned no documents (status no_data; this shows only that the query matched nothing), while the index only holds payment-service-us, payment-service-eu and payment-service-ap; the exact name 'payment-service' therefore has no log evidence, and its relationship to the three regional identities is unknown.

The index documents contain no cluster/region/environment field and no HTTP status/500 record, so neither the owning cluster of payment-service-us/-eu/-ap nor an actual 500 response is evidenced; only the four ERROR texts are.

Cause of the payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d container restart (exitCode 255, reason Unknown, 08:04:13Z, restartCount 2) is unknown; the previous container's log stream returned 0 lines and no event mentions this pod, and no evidence ties that restart to the index errors.
Whether flagd flags were overridden at runtime during the window is unknown: only the static ConfigMap demo.flagd.json was read, flagd's runtime state/API was not queried.
No logs, metrics or traces exist in the available sources for the upstream providers stripe-us and adyen-eu, so their availability and the response-time of stripe-us are unverified.
Change history is not integrated in this Run, so a configuration or credential change around 07:59:33Z/08:59:33Z for payment-service-us or payment-service-eu cannot be checked.

Two Warning events failed to create Endpoints for 'orca' and 'signup-service' (namespace not shown) inside the window; they name objects that could not be read and were not tied to the payment errors.

content:
groups:
- name: opspilot-lab
  rules:
  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
